title: Banging two toys together shows up by nine months on the CDC list
summary: By about nine months, most babies bang two things together, the U.S. CDC says, counting only a skill that at least three quarters of children show.
body: Under cognitive milestones, the CDC 9-month sheet names banging two things together. A milestone, on that sheet, is something most children, 75 percent or more, can do by the age printed. The sheet adds that Learn the Signs. Act Early. materials are not a substitute for standardized, validated developmental screening tools. Failing to bang toys is not a diagnosis of one baby, and a list printed outside the United States can name other skills. Searching for a spoon that fell out of sight is a different line on the same sheet and is not this claim.

sources.title: Milestones by 9-months

sources.note: CDC Learn the Signs. Act Early. page, U.S. government work, public domain. Updated and reviewed 16 May 2026. Supports banging two things together as a cognitive milestone most babies do by 9 months.
